supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:34, ana.ruiz ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-PIN-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ana.ruiz\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that archive at 13:44:38.

At 13:50:57, the proxy recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server tunnel from WS-ARUIZ-01 to dropzone-transfer.net, attributed to ana.ruiz and Firefox. Zeek independently recorded 51,000,372 originating bytes for the corresponding proxy connection.

The archive creation and large outbound transfer occur within minutes of one another, and the destination is not among the approved services listed in the environment context. This sequence supports a finding of likely data exfiltration, although the available records do not prove the archive was the transferred payload.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec collection was unavailable on DC-PIN-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, limiting domain-controller authentication and audit visibility during that interval.
The proxy records the destination, user, tunnel byte counts, and duration, but this transfer is logged as a tunnel; the available records do not show the uploaded filename or payload.
The prominent large transfer in the records occurred at 13:50:57 UTC, several minutes after the alert's approximate 13:46 time.
claims_not_established: The contents of c.zip and whether it contained sensitive client data.
Whether c.zip was the payload sent to dropzone-transfer.net, or whether the large transfer contained other data.
Who initiated or authorized the activity, and whether the user had a legitimate business purpose.
Whether the approximate alert time refers to the observed 13:50:57 transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover and preserve c.zip and relevant endpoint file-system or forensic evidence, including its size, hash, contents, and creation/access history.
Obtain proxy or destination-side details that identify the request path, upload metadata, and payload if available.
Confirm with ana.ruiz and the relevant data owner whether the archive and transfer were authorized.
Review domain-controller audit data for the outage window if recoverable.
unrelated_findings: Dropbox.exe was launched by ana.ruiz, and a subsequent proxy connection used the DropboxUpdate user agent to reach desktop.dropbox.com. Dropbox is not listed among approved services; investigate separately. (T099-00239, T099-00241, T099-00247, T099-00248)
ana.ruiz ran PowerShell to query AD users in the IT OU. This is separate from the alerted transfer and merits contextual review. (T099-00433, T099-00434)

PROXY-PIN-01 initiated an RPC connection to WS-ARUIZ-01 on port 135. The supplied IT practices describe remote administration from WS-RPATEL-01; investigate this separately without treating it as evidence for the alerted transfer. (T099-00110, T099-00111, T099-00112, T099-00113)
